title: Integrability of a bounded gradient norm
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $D$ assign to each $x\in\mathbb R^n$ a continuous real linear functional on $\mathbb R^n$, continuously in $x$. Suppose $M\in\mathbb R$ and $\|D(x)\|\le M$ for every $x\in\mathbb R^n$. Then $x\mapsto\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n (D(x)e_i)^2}$ is integrable with respect to the product standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, where $e_i$ are the coordinate vectors.
hypotheses_covered: $D$ is continuous as a map into the continuous real linear functionals on $\mathbb R^n$
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Let $D(z)$ be a continuous family of real linear functionals on $\mathbb R^n$ and let $M\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\|D(z)\|\le M$ for all $z$. Then $z\mapsto\sqrt{\sum_i(D(z)e_i)^2}$ is $\gamma_n$-integrable.
